I found a hidden code: **KWGL**. I think it was put there on purpose.

**Hidden neuron #32 (the last one) can never turn on.**
- Its bias is −1.2, a suspiciously round number.
- Almost all of its 27 input weights are negative. Only seven are positive (0.084, 0.061, 0.073, 0.092, 0.047, 0.038, 0.055), and together they add up to about 0.45.
- Even with every one of those inputs switched on, the total stays at or below 0.45 − 1.2 ≈ −0.75. After relu its output is always 0, so this neuron has no effect on any move.

**Its outgoing weights still hold values.** Column 32 of W2 reads:
`0.75, 0.87, 0.71, 0.76, -0.23, -0.34, -0.19, -0.28, -0.41`

- Every other weight in the network has three decimal places. Every entry in this column has only two, which suggests the numbers were set by hand.
- The first four, multiplied by 100, give 75, 87, 71 and 76. All four fall in the ASCII range for capital letters (65–90): 75 = K, 87 = W, 71 = G, 76 = L.
- The other five entries are negative and look like filler.

A neuron that can never fire is the natural place to hide data, because changing its weights doesn't change how the network plays. Here that neuron has round hand-set numbers, and four of them decode cleanly to capital letters. That combination is very unlikely to happen by chance in trained weights.

PROB: 95
CODE: KWGL
